A church leader in Coventry, United Kingdom, Brein Ayeni, has been sentenced to 11 years and nine months in prison for raping a woman and subjecting her to coercive and controlling behaviour. Ayeni, 43, who headed the Christworld Nation Church in Coventry, was convicted of three counts of rape and one count of coercive or controlling behaviour following a trial. West Midlands Police disclosed this in a statement published on its website on Monday. The offences reportedly began in June 2025, with the church leader recording some of the attacks on his mobile phone. According to the police, Ayeni threatened to share the videos if the woman reported the abuse, claiming they showed that what happened was consensual. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He also made derogatory comments about her, comparing her previous lifestyle choices to poison, and displayed controlling behaviour after gaining her trust. The woman reported the abuse to the police in March 2026, prompting an investigation by specialist officers from the force’s Rape and Serious Sexual Offences team. Ayeni, who lived on Hurst Road, Coventry, was sentenced at Warwick Crown Court on November 10. In a victim impact statement, the woman said the abuse had severely affected her ability to trust others and her mental and emotional well-being. The impact on my mental and emotional health is that I do not feel like the same person I was before all of this happened. “I struggle to trust people and allow them to get close to me because I am frightened of being taken advantage of again. It has affected my family, who have had to watch someone they love go through something so painful. “I understand how frightening it can be to speak up when you know that people may question you, judge you or turn against you. Reporting what happened took courage. It was not easy for me, and I have had to fight through fear, uncertainty and the emotional weight of revisiting these experiences. “I am grateful for the people who have supported me. I do not want another woman to experience the fear, confusion, humiliation and emotional pain that I have had to live with.” Detective Sergeant Evie Griffiths, of the force’s public protection unit, described the offences as horrific and said they had left a lasting impact on the victim. Griffiths said, “These were horrific crimes which have understandably had a lasting impact. It is through her bravery in telling us what happened we were able to arrest Ayeni and stop him committing any further offences. “We never underestimate the harm and distress caused by sex attackers which is why we have specially-trained officers who work tirelessly to catch offenders and support those who have been attacked. “Ayeni abused the trust in him to carry out these terrible crimes, but he has quite rightly been put behind bars for a significant period of time. “We hope she can use the strength from knowing her bravery has helped protect herself, and others, from Ayeni will assist in continuing her recovery from this truly awful ordeal.” Saheed Oyelakin Saheed is a journalist at Punch Newspapers with over two years of experience covering metro, technology, sports, politics, and human-interest stories.
